newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up, further gains expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 2.97 percent on Monday and market participants forecast persistent demand from foreign investors would fuel further price rises.
"The feeling on the market is still very optimistic," said Simona Lebar a trader at Eastbrokers. She added that the market looked to have enough momentum to take prices higher this week.
"There may be some slight falls, but only as a technical reaction to recent big jumps," Lebar said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 32.62 points to 1,129.74.
* 13 shares rose and six fell, while three were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 609.9 million tolars from 560 million.
* Bank SKB shares were the most actively traded, firming 7.96 percent to 37,346 tolars on volume of 7,647 shares for total turnover of 285.6 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska banka were the biggest gainer, firming 10 percent to 12,100 tolars on volume of 55 shares for total turnover of 666,000 tolars.l

* Construction company GPG was the leading decliner, falling 8.84 percent to 8,000 tolars on volume of 5,108 shares for total turnover of 40.9 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
